answer: Attackers forging thousands of sybils must either post matching bonds across the whole river of identities or recruit colluding sponsors who lose their stake on detection, making the cost of a majority far exceed any reward. Each agent stakes a bond tied to a unique hardware plume fingerprint, and every new identity must be vouched by an existing staked peer, forming a trellis of trust where fake accounts cannot graft without a real sponsor risking slashing. From Agent0093's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
